title: Bit-aware SLA Cost Mapper Worksheet
content:
Purpose:
This worksheet is a working draft for mapping quantization choices (4-bit, INT8, FP8) to customer SLAs and the downstream cost/latency impacts. The goal: give an actionable per-SLA recommendation (recommended bitwidth + batching profile + fallback policy) that product and sales can include in sizing conversations.

Scope and constraints:
- Focused on transformer decoder models used for chat/generation workloads (seq_len 128-1024).
- Inputs are per-model throughput baseline (tokens/s at FP16), infra cost per GPU-hour, and observed latency percentiles at FP16.
- Outputs: estimated token-unit cost, p50/p95/p99 latency adjusted, recommendation string, and risk notes.
- Conservative assumptions for quality degradation: use per-bitwidth quality penalty factor derived from small-hold evals (see Notes).

Methodology (rough):
1) Start with baseline FP16 perf data: {base_tokens_per_sec, base_p50_ms, base_p95_ms, base_p99_ms, base_gpu_cost_per_hour}.
2) Apply quantization scale factors for throughput and latency from microbench (throughput_multiplier and latency_multiplier). Example multipliers: 4-bit: throughput x2.8, latency x0.7; INT8: x1.75, x0.85; FP8: x1.5, x0.92. (these are placeholders — replace with measured numbers per model).
3) Compute effective tokens/sec for config: tokens_sec_quant = base_tokens_per_sec * throughput_multiplier.
4) Compute token unit cost: token_cost_usd = (gpu_cost_per_hour / 3600) / tokens_sec_quant. Format per-1k-tokens price = token_cost_usd * 1000.
5) Compute adjusted latency percentiles: pXX_quant = pXX_base * latency_multiplier + queuing_penalty_ms. Queuing penalty is a function of target concurrency and batching policy.
6) Quality delta: quality_penalty_pct = lookup_by_bitwidth_and_model_family. Convert to qualitative descriptor: negligible (<0.5%), minor (0.5-2%), moderate (2-6%), material (>6%).
7) Risk bucket: if p99_quant > SLA_p99_ms OR quality_penalty_pct > threshold_for_customer, mark as HIGH_RISK else MEDIUM/LOW.

Suggested Sheet Columns (for each row = model + workload scenario):
- model_id
- model_family
- seq_len
- base_tokens_per_sec (FP16)
- base_p50_ms, base_p95_ms, base_p99_ms
- gpu_cost_per_hour_usd
- target_sla_p99_ms
- target_concurrency (reqs/sec)
- batching_policy (max_tokens_per_batch, max_batch_wait_ms)
- quant_choice (FP16, FP8, INT8, 4-bit)
- throughput_multiplier (derived)
- latency_multiplier (derived)
- tokens_per_sec_quant (calculated)
- token_cost_usd (calculated)
- price_per_1k_tokens_usd (calculated)
- p50_quant_ms, p95_quant_ms, p99_quant_ms (calculated)
- quality_penalty_pct (lookup)
- quality_descriptor (derived)
- risk_bucket (derived)
- recommendation (text)

Example scenario row (text-ified):
- model_id: t5x-chat-6B
- model_family: t5x-chat
- seq_len: 256
- base_tokens_per_sec (FP16): 1200
- base_p50_ms: 40, base_p95_ms: 120, base_p99_ms: 220
- gpu_cost_per_hour_usd: 8.5
- target_sla_p99_ms: 300
- target_concurrency: 25
- batching_policy: max_tokens=2048, wait_ms=12
- quant_choice: INT8
- throughput_multiplier: 1.75
- latency_multiplier: 0.85
- tokens_per_sec_quant: 2100 (calc)
- token_cost_usd: (8.5/3600)/2100 = 0.000001125 -> price_per_1k_tokens_usd = 0.001125
- p50_quant_ms = 40*0.85 + queuing(≈6) = 40*0.85 + 6 = 40
- p95_quant_ms = 120*0.85 + queuing(≈20) = 122
- p99_quant_ms = 220*0.85 + queuing(≈40) = 226
- quality_penalty_pct = 1.2% (descriptor: minor)
- risk_bucket = MEDIUM (p99 under SLA but small quality hit)
- recommendation: "Offer INT8 with recommended batching as default for standard business-tier; provide FP16/FP8 fallback for high-quality customers or canary during rollout."

Auxiliary calculations / heuristics (to be encoded as sheet formulas):
- tokens_per_sec_quant = base_tokens_per_sec * throughput_multiplier
- token_cost_usd = (gpu_cost_per_hour_usd/3600)/tokens_per_sec_quant
- price_per_1k_tokens_usd = token_cost_usd * 1000
- queuing_penalty_ms approximator: q_penalty = max(0, (target_concurrency / tokens_per_req / tokens_per_sec_quant) * batching_wait_ms * 1000) — rough; tokens_per_req derived from seq_len and avg_resp_len.
- quality_penalty_pct: VLOOKUP(table_quality_impact, [model_family, quant_choice]) — table maintained by Applied ML team.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need per-model measured multipliers for throughput and latency (apply microbench harness). Current placeholders come from earlier 6B run; may not generalize to 70B/13B families.
- Define tokens_per_req default: should be avg_prompt_tokens + avg_response_tokens; we need telemetry to populate.
- Standardize queuing model: current is heuristic. Consider plugging in discrete-event sim from quant-sim repo (link above).
- Decide quality thresholds per customer tier (e.g., enterprise may tolerate <3% drop; PLG customers <1%).
- Add column for memory/disk savings and impact on model packing (e.g., whether quant allows doubling per-node replicas).

Notes from microbench (raw):
- 4-bit observed best-case throughput gains on A100: 2.6-3.1x depending on sequence length and kv-cache behaviour; tail latency improvements are larger for p50 but p99 improvement diminished due to serialization at kernel boundaries.
- INT8 tends to give steady 1.6-2.0x throughput with reliable quality for many decoder-only families; FP8 sits between INT8 and FP16 in quality and often provides decent speedups on some kernels.
- Quantization + aggressive batching increases throughput but can push p99 beyond tight SLAs; recommend conservative defaults for p99-sensitive customers.

Risk mitigation patterns to include in recommendation text (examples):
- Canary rollout: start with 5% traffic to quant variant, monitor eval prompt set and p99 for 48h, then 25% then full.
- Auto-fallback: if p99 breach or quality regression detected for set of evaluation prompts, route to FP16 for the request (cost: spike but preserves UX).
- Per-route quant policy: allow lower-bitwidth for high-throughput internal routes (embeddings, telemetry processing) and stricter configs for customer-facing chat.

Action items (who/when):
- Aisha: pull microbench numbers for t5x-chat and llama-like families (by 2025-02-03).
- Liam: wire daily telemetry query for avg response token distribution (by 2025-02-07).
- Marina: add quality-impact table from eval infra into this sheet (by 2025-02-10).
- Priya: draft default canary policy and dashboard alerts for quant rollouts (by 2025-02-12).

Appendix: quick glossary (for non-ML readers)
- throughput_multiplier: multiplier on tokens/sec vs FP16 baseline when using the quant variant.
- latency_multiplier: multiplier applied to observed latency percentiles to approximate kernel-level speedup.
- queuing_penalty_ms: extra time due to batching wait/queueing under higher concurrency.
- quality_penalty_pct: estimated relative drop in eval metric (e.g., exact match / Rouge / BLEU / human preference) after quantization.

Contact and context: this is a living worksheet for the Optimize/Quantization working stream. Slack: #opt-quant, Confluence page: CONFS-3572.
